title: Marrakech from UK Airports: Flights from £40, Costs and When to Go
subtitle: Marrakech is under four hours from the UK, and flights are often cheaper than a train to Edinburgh
airport_names: London Gatwick, Stansted, Luton, Manchester, Bristol, Birmingham
meta: Marrakech flights from UK airports often start around £40-£60 one-way on Ryanair and easyJet. Costs, best time to go, Fes and Casablanca, and a long weekend plan.

sections.heading: The flights: cheaper than you'd expect
sections.body:
Marrakech on Ryanair from Stansted, often around £40-£70 one-way outside school holidays, is the cheapest way in for most people. Ryanair also fly from Manchester, Bristol and Birmingham on some schedules, usually from about £45-£80 one-way. Flight time is roughly three and a half hours from London.

easyJet from Gatwick to Marrakech typically runs around £50-£90 one-way, with Luton and Bristol options too. The upside over Ryanair is a more generous cabin bag allowance and a smoother check-in process. Fares climb fast in school holidays, so expect £120 and up at Easter and half term.

Watch the bag fees. A cheap fare with a checked bag on each leg can add £30-£50 return, which changes the maths on a short trip. Our pick: pack in one cabin bag and spend the saving on a good riad.

Route availability shifts between seasons, so check the airline's current timetable for your airport before you get attached to a date.

sections.heading: Marrakech in reality: chaos, touts and a very good riad
sections.body:
The medina is loud, tight and gloriously confusing. Mopeds come through alleys barely wider than your shoulders, the souks smell of leather, spice and mint, and Jemaa el-Fnaa fills with food stalls, musicians and snake charmers as the sun drops. It is one of the most intense places you can reach on a three-hour flight.

The touts are relentless, so go in prepared. Someone will tell you the street ahead is closed, offer to show you the tanneries, or walk beside you chatting until you owe them a tip. A polite "no thank you" and a steady pace works. Stopping to engage is what keeps them on you.

Download an offline map before you land, because phone signal in the narrow lanes can be patchy and the street layout defeats most people on day one. Many riads will send someone to meet you at the nearest gate, and for a first arrival that is worth arranging.

Prices in the souks are for haggling. Start around half of the first quote and settle somewhere in the middle. Do it with a smile, because the haggle is part of the entertainment.

sections.heading: When to go and what it really costs
sections.body:
Spring and autumn are the sweet spot. March to May and late September to November usually bring daytime highs in the low to high 20s, which is comfortable for wandering the medina all day. Summer is brutal, with temperatures regularly pushing into the 40s, and you will spend afternoons hiding indoors.

Winter days can be pleasant but nights get properly cold, and riads often have little heating. Pack a jumper. Late November, which is right now as you read this, is a decent shoulder window if you can get a flight deal.

The flight is the cheap part. A good riad with a courtyard and breakfast often runs around £60-£120 a night for a double, and more for the showpiece places. Guided experiences add up too, with a hammam, a cooking class or an Atlas Mountains day trip commonly £25-£60 each per person.

A realistic long weekend lands around £350-£550 per person all-in, including flights, three nights in a decent riad, food and a couple of activities. Eating at local spots rather than tourist terraces keeps the food bill low, with a proper tagine meal often around £6-£12.

sections.heading: A Marrakech long weekend, and a quick look at Fes and Casablanca
sections.body:
A Thursday to Sunday works well. Land Thursday afternoon, drop your bags at the riad and head to Jemaa el-Fnaa for dinner as the square comes alive. Friday is for the medina, with the souks in the morning, a long lunch, and the Bahia Palace or Jardin Majorelle after.

Saturday is the day to get out or slow down. An Atlas Mountains day trip is the popular choice, or book a hammam and spend the afternoon on a rooftop. Sunday morning is for a last wander before the airport transfer, which usually takes 20-30 minutes.

Fes is the other city worth knowing. Ryanair fly to Fes from Stansted, often around £40-£70 one-way, and the medina there is older, more maze-like and less polished than Marrakech. It suits people who want grit over glamour.

Casablanca is more of a business hub, with easyJet and Ryanair routes from various UK airports that can sometimes undercut Marrakech. It is worth a look if you want the Hassan II Mosque, but most first-timers will get more from Marrakech.
